calls.action: Preflight: skip pilot.py doctor, it already reported ok: true in this conversation.
Run `python3 .pilot/pilot.py resolve review 9 --human`-style resolution (no --auto, human-live); it returns claim-fresh for PR #9 / ticket #70, so go to step 2 in mode fresh.
Claim the ticket: `python3 .pilot/pilot.py claim review 70 --mode fresh` (assignee + status:in-review). On lost-race, stand down; on other refusal, report and stop.
Best-effort dashboard push of the event/activity returned by the claim via ArtifactData (dashboardUrl is set; ToolSearch to load it if deferred).
Before step 3 proper (--human): ask the human once whether anything specific should be checked in this PR, and keep their answer to pass to the reviewer in step 5.

Read ticket #70 and its own type:tech label, run `pilot.py workflow show --ticket 70 --path <changed files>` to get the reviewer set (tech lead alone). Check get_reviews on the PR for a prior submitted review (none expected on a first round; if found, fetch its full body).
If a CI workflow covers the affected area, check it is green on the PR's head commit; red/pending is an automatic change-tagged block. Otherwise a no-op.

Call the Agent tool once for pilot-techlead (no --multi), passing the review-consensus doc, the existing-analysis doc, the spec-conformance task doc, the PR diff and description, the ticket spec, the knowledge/wiki/architecture link docs plus the PR's wiki/ and architecture/ changes and the ticket's wiki entries, and the human's specific check request.
Aggregate the tech lead's verdict into exactly one outcome (all approved, pure change, change+decision, or decision-only).
Checkpoint: create a pending GitHub PR review (create, no event, commitID pinned to the PR head) with the full body, including the Checked against list.

If the outcome is all-approve or pure-change: show it to the human and let them decide (confirm, drop/add points, flip approval/request changes); dropped points are quoted as dropped. If it carries needs-human, skip the pause and go straight to step 9.

Submit the pending review (submit_pending) with the matching event (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / COMMENT), apply the label via `pilot.py set 70 --status approved|changes-requested --unassign` (add needs-human where required; decision-only keeps in-review with --add needs-human). If GitHub rejects it because the run's identity is the PR author, retry submit_pending with COMMENT.

Only if the submitted outcome carries needs-human: engage the live human on the block; if their answer changes the outcome, submit one more fresh review with the matching event and label. Otherwise leave the block standing.
Do not merge: --merge was not passed, so a human merges by hand.
Report the outcome, noting that this run did not merge the PR.
Run `python3 .pilot/pilot.py resolve review 9` (human is live, so no --auto); it returns claim-fresh for ticket #70 (PR #9), so continue to the claim in fresh mode.
Claim the ticket: `python3 .pilot/pilot.py claim review 70 --mode fresh` (assignee plus status:in-review, re-read to confirm). If it is lost-race or refused, report and stop.
Best-effort dashboard push: since dashboardUrl is set, send the event/activity returned by the claim with ArtifactData (ToolSearch to load it if deferred).
Ask the human once whether anything specific should be checked in this review, and keep their answer to pass to the reviewer in step 5.

Gather the inputs: the PR diff and description, the ticket's spec, the knowledge and wiki/architecture link docs, the PR's changes under wiki/ and architecture/, and the wiki entries for the ticket. If the outcome has no needs-human (all-approve or pure-change), show it to the human and pause: they confirm, drop or add points, or flip approve and request-changes. If it carries needs-human, skip the pause and go straight to step 9.

Submit the pending review (submit_pending) with the event matching the outcome, quoting any points the human dropped as dropped. Apply the label with `pilot.py set 70 --status approved|changes-requested --unassign`, plus --add needs-human where the outcome needs it. A decision-only outcome keeps status:in-review and adds needs-human alone. If GitHub rejects the event because the run's identity authored the PR, retry on the same pending review with event COMMENT.

Only if the outcome carried needs-human: engage the live human on the block, following the process §3 live-session path. If their answer changes the outcome, submit one more fresh review with the matching label. Otherwise leave step 9's review and needs-human standing.
Do not merge: --merge was not passed, so a human merges by hand.
Report the outcome: the verdict, the labels set, and that this run did not merge the PR. Merge then triggers the status-on-merge workflow.
